tutorial.text: Welcome! This tool helps you explore Pareto-optimal portfolios find solutions within objective ranges, discover correlations between objectives and decisions, and make an informed choice about the best trade-off. The header guides you through the tutorial and tasks. Use the sidebar to toggle between frontiers.
This is the Objectives Space. Each point is a portfolio on the Pareto frontier, representing an optimal trade-off between objectives.
This is the Decision Space. It maps each solution to its decision variable allocations.

Every chart supports hovering, selection, and filtering. Hold Shift + click a point to select it selections are synchronized between both spaces. Each chart type adds its own custom interactions, shown as we go.
Both spaces offer several visualisation types. We'll walk through each one, explaining their functionality.
The 2D Scatterplot shows the relationship between two objectives. Use the axis dropdowns to change what's plotted. Shift + click to select a point, or use the Lasso Tool to select an area.
Click Options to customise the scatterplot. Toggle Dim. Reduction (PCA), Labels, Dominant Dec. Groups, or Frontier Colours.
The 3D Scatterplot adds a third axis. Click and drag to rotate. Brush (click and drag) along any axis to filter portfolios to a range. Deselect by double-clicking the axis or using Clear Selection.
Click Options for 3D extras: Surface renders the Pareto frontier as a mesh, Dominated shows non-optimal solutions, and Ideal Point marks the theoretical best.

The Parallel Coordinates Plot draws each objective as a vertical axis; each portfolio is a line crossing all axes. Brush (click and drag) an axis to filter to a range. Deselect by double-clicking the axis or using Clear Selection.
Click Options to colour lines by Dec. Groups or Frontier Colours.
The Radar Chart maps each objective onto a radial axis; each portfolio is drawn as a polygon. Brush an axis to filter portfolios. Deselect by double-clicking the axis or using Clear Selection.
Click Options to colour polygons by Dec. Groups or Frontier Colours.

RadViz positions each portfolio based on its pull towards objective anchors around the circle. Balanced portfolios land near the centre; those excelling in one objective are pulled to its anchor. Shift + click or use the Lasso Tool to select.

Each portfolio is shown as a mini pie glyph. Click it to expand into a full donut chart of asset composition. Click a group arc to drill into individual assets in the inner ring. Click the empty area to close.
Click Options to toggle Spread (redistributes points into a grid) or Frontier Colours.

The Correlation Heatmap shows pairwise correlations between objectives. Dark = negative correlation; light = positive. Use it to identify which objectives/decision variables move together or pull against each other.
The Column Chart shows decision variable values as grouped bars, one bar per portfolio. Useful for comparing absolute allocations across all solutions.
Groups like Real Assets contain multiple assets. Click on a group bar to expand and see individual asset allocations.

The Table lists every portfolio with its raw objective and decision values. Sort by any column. Brush the mini bars at the top to filter portfolios to a range, deselect by using Clear Selection or by double-cliking the filter.
Groups like Fixed Income in the table columns can be expanded to show individual assets.
